newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: OLYMPICS-CAPE TOWN OLYMPIC BID HAMPERED BY CRIME PROBLEM.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-CAPE TOWN OLYMPIC BID HAMPERED BY CRIME PROBLEM.

text.p: Cape Town, one of the early favourites to host the 2004 Olympics, has had its bid to stage Africa's first Summer Games hampered by a rampant crime problem, according to the International Olympic Committee's evaluation report on Thursday.
Although there was no clear favourite among the 11 candidate cities in the IOC report, Athens and Rome received positive assessments, confirming them as front-runners.
The IOC said five final cities from 11 candidates would be announced at the body's meeting on March 7 in Lausanne. The winner will be named on September 5.
Athens, which felt it was snubbed by the IOC in its bid to host the 1996 Centennial Olympics, received a generally favourable report.

The IOC praised Athens's efforts to alleviate pollution but said the city had significant problems with airport access and transportation. However, extensive improvements were under way. It made no specific mention of security problems and terrorism in Athens, which were major concerns in its earlier bid.

The IOC said many first-class facilities were in place in Rome. Although traffic was a major problem in the Italian capital, as in Athens, the IOC said it believed planning was being done to meet the transportation challenge.
The other bidding cities are Buenos Aires, Istanbul, Lille, Rio de Janeiro, San Juan, Seville, Stockholm and St Petersburg.
